native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (ever_jailed, jailed 1985-1994) had significantly lower wealth than those without in ALL three observed years: 1985, 1990, and 1996. Median wealth jailed vs non-jailed: $720 vs $3,600 (1985), $0 vs $10,500 (1990), $0 vs $8,500 (1996). One-sided Mann-Whitney U p = 8.0e-11 / 3.9e-35 / 4.6e-26, all below both alpha=0.05 and Bonferroni threshold 0.0167 (corrected p = 2.4e-10 / 1.2e-34 / 1.4e-25); effect sizes (Z/sqrt(N)) = -0.058 / -0.112 / -0.093 (negative = jailed lower). Sign consistent across median (quantile) regression and OLS on winsorized and log-shifted wealth with race/sex controls (negative significant ever_jailed coefficient in all years). Caveat: wealth-1985 may be measured before incarceration for some respondents, so this is a robust association, not established causation.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected data (12,013 rows, no missing values; ever_jailed 289 vs 11,724). 2) Primary: one-sided Mann-Whitney U per year (1985/1990/1996), H1 = jailed wealth lower; reported medians/means, U, z, raw p, Bonferroni-corrected p (3 tests, threshold 0.0167), effect sizes r=Z/sqrt(N). 3) Robustness: median (quantile) regression wealth ~ ever_jailed + race + sex; OLS on winsorized wealth (clip 99th pct) with same controls; OLS on log(wealth - min + 1) with same controls. 4) Conclusion: years where one-sided p < 0.05 (and < 0.0167) AND sign consistent across all checks -> all three years 1985, 1990, 1996.

sub_hypo.text: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, with wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Individuals jailed between 1985 and 1994 (ever_jailed = 1) have significantly lower composite wealth in each of 1985, 1990, and 1996 than those not jailed during that period (ever_jailed = 0).

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals jailed between 1985 and 1994 had significantly lower wealth than non-jailed individuals in all three observed years: 1985, 1990, and 1996. This association remained negative and significant with race and sex controls across robustness checks, but does not establish causation.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979 cohort; 12,013 respondents with no missing values, including 289 jailed between 1985 and 1994 and 11,724 non-jailed respondents; wealth observed in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed respondents had lower median wealth than non-jailed respondents: $720 versus $3,600 in 1985, $0 versus $10,500 in 1990, and $0 versus $8,500 in 1996. Respective one-sided Mann-Whitney U p-values were 8.0e-11, 3.9e-35, and 4.6e-26, all below alpha=0.05 and the Bonferroni threshold of 0.0167; corrected p-values were 2.4e-10, 1.2e-34, and 1.4e-25. Effect sizes r=Z/sqrt(N) were -0.058, -0.112, and -0.093, respectively, indicating lower wealth among jailed respondents. The ever_jailed coefficient was negative and significant in every year in median regression and OLS on wealth winsorized at the 99th percentile and on log(wealth - min + 1), controlling for race and sex. This is a robust association rather than established causation because 1985 wealth may precede incarceration for some respondents.
